name: MANU (Genoa)
full_name: MANU Genoa rhenium-187 calorimetric neutrino-mass experiment
summary: MANU was a pioneering direct neutrino-mass experiment in Genoa using a metallic rhenium absorber at very low temperature. It is the historical experiment labelled GENOVA in the supplied map.
detection_principle: A small rhenium crystal absorbs the beta-decay energy, and an attached germanium thermistor measures the thermal pulse. Fitting the calorimetric endpoint spectrum constrains the escaping antineutrino mass.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The experimental review documents the pioneering MANU calorimeter and its published 2001 mass analysis.

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: The experimental review documents the pioneering MANU calorimeter and its published 2001 mass analysis.

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
